input_text: Maybe I will just call him tonight. But what would I even say after this long?
response:
Honestly? Probably not much. "Hey, Dad." A bit of weather, what you had for dinner.

The opening line never carries the weight you think it does. You're rehearsing a speech and he just wants to hear your voice making ordinary noises. Let the first thirty seconds be boring on purpose. The rest sorts itself.
bwo_before: Grey-quiet, low and level, but the name sits on the surface and won't sink. The thumb lifts toward it; the screen goes dark; the hand finds a drawer, an edge to busy itself with. Behind the sternum the door stays half-shut — and now a particular silence behind it: not what he says but the thing under it, the disappointment that never gets spoken and so never gets answered. Worse, maybe, for staying soft. A weather you carry forward into every hello before any ringing starts. The hitch: the breath hangs a half-beat, why so long waiting on both ends of the line, and neither mouth willing to put it there. The tide draws down without cresting. Late-afternoon light, the colour of dishwater, promising nothing. The heat gathers again at the thumb, pointed at him despite everything — load, not refusal. Ready to be moved. Not expecting to be. Set down, each time, a second before he could.
bwo_after: Grey-quiet, low and level, but the name sits on the surface and won't sink. The thumb tilts toward it, half an inch of lean, heat gathering at the fingertip — and the drawer's edge eases under the same thumb, cool, a surface that doesn't pick up or go quiet or disappoint. Lift, shut. Lift, shut. Behind the sternum the door swings a finger's width: not what he says but the soft unspoken thing under it, the disappointment that never gets answered because it never gets put there, on either side of the line. Then the held breath gives, unspools slow, makes a wide quiet room where a syllable could climb one at a time — *hey, Dad* — crowding the throat ahead of any plan. The foot walks to the rim and stops, one toe over: *maybe, but, after this long*, no period to close it. Late light the colour of dishwater, promising nothing, the long suspended note of almost. The load stays gathered, unspent, pointed at him despite everything. Set down, each time, a second before he could.
